# Installing Quanteda package and the rest of necessary libraries

```{r}
install.packages("readtext")
library(quanteda)
library(readtext)
library(tidyverse)

```

#Importing my article text dataframe
```{r}
articles <- read_csv("articles_df.csv")
```

# Creating my_corpus using the 'sentence' column as the text field

```{r}
my_corpus <- corpus(articles, text_field = "sentence") 
head(my_corpus)


```

## KWIC search. The keywords and phrases are chosen in quanteda_test2 table. I decided with these words because I wanted to see what kind of testimonies, type of activism women from Xinjiang do. Because most of the time the testimonies are related to the violation of reproductive and other types of human rights, I made sure to include it. I could potentially do the wild card with that as well but decided against it as the word "reproductive" usually goes in exact same spelling in majority of testimonies. 

```{r}

# Tokenize the corpus
my_tokens <- tokens(my_corpus)

# Perform KWIC (Key Word in Context) search on the tokens
quanteda_test <- kwic(my_tokens, pattern = "women", valuetype = "regex") %>% 
  as.data.frame()

quanteda_test2 <- kwic(my_tokens, phrase(c("women", "Uyghur women", "Kazakh women", "Xinjiang women", "reproductive", "abortion", "sterilization", "human rights", "testimony", "activism")), window = 14, valuetype = "regex") %>% as.data.frame() 

write.csv(quanteda_test, "quanteda_test.csv")

```



# Housecleaning was not necessary for my KWIC search because it found words exactly as I typed them. I checked all the rows. 
```{r}
#cut useless returns
#XJjunk <- c("NA")
#kwic_with_metadata <- kwic_with_metadata %>%
  #filter(!keyword %in% XJjunk)


#Eliminate duplication
kwic_with_metadata  <- kwic_with_metadata  %>% 
  distinct(docname, pre, keyword, post, newspaper_name, date, url) %>% 
  rename('Beginning of Passage' = pre, 'End of Passage' = post, Newspaper = newspaper_name, Date = date) 

kwic_with_metadata_csv <- kwic_with_metadata  %>%
  add_column(Code = NA) %>% 
  add_column(Comments = NA) %>% 
  select(docname, Newspaper, Date, 'Beginning of Passage', keyword, 'End of Passage', Code, Comments)

#write_csv(kwic_with_metadata_csv, "../exercises/assets/data/kwic_with_metadata.csv")

```

#Memo 255 words

KWIC search provided a quick, useful way to find relevant texts that match my keywords. It was impressive to see that keyword search found relevant words without being distorted by other words, as in the class example with "mob" and "mobility". 

One thing I would do differently is avoid using a generic word, such as "women", in keyword searches because it might return irrelevant results. In my case, the texts that had "women" in them talked about the employment rate of women, or articles of propagandistic nature that claim Xinjiang women's emancipation and modernization from their "backward" culture. The word "reproductive" also found some positive-leaning articles that stated that "reproductive rights and their family status have significantly improved," or articles about "reproductive health services," that are not related to women's testimonies. This is not a big issue, and human oversight is always needed to analyze this kind of keyword search. On the other hand, stronger keywords, such as “sterilization(s)”, “abortion(s)” have returned more relevant results. The word “testimony” also found the articles that I was looking for. However, sometimes those keywords appeared in articles from Chinese media that claim the allegations are false. 

Overall, KWIC search seems quite useful for finding articles with certain angles. I found that 15 words before and after the keyword is a good middle ground for reading the full sentence context and understanding how those keywords are used. Previous attempts using 10 words were not successful, while 50 words showed too much irrelevant text around the main keyword.
